JironFormBuilder.description: Jiron Form Builder's host configuration: the JironFormBuilder section of appsettings. It is for developers and for locks, and it wins over the backoffice. It is read once and checked when the site starts: a value out of range or a key Jiron Form Builder does not know stops the site with a message that names the key, and a change takes effect when the site restarts.

PublicApi.description: The public API visitors' browsers and headless sites call: where it lives and who may call it.

BasePath.description: The path the API lives under, before its version (/v1): / and one or more segments of letters, digits, '.', '-', '_' and '~', at most 100 characters in all, and neither /umbraco, /App_Plugins or /jfb/assets nor a path below or above one of them.

AllowedOrigins.description: The other sites whose pages may call the API from the browser, each an origin such as https://www.example.com: http or https, a host and a port when it is not the scheme's, and nothing after them. The site's own pages may always call it. None by default.

ServerKeys.description: The keys headless servers submit with, sending Authorization: Jfb-Key <key>: a name and the SHA-256 of each key, never the key. None by default.

items.description: A headless server's key, by its name and the SHA-256 of the key.

Name.description: The key's name, which an entry the key submits records as its context value jfbServerKey: 1 to 64 letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, each name once.

Sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the key's UTF-8 bytes as 64 hexadecimal digits, each hash once; scripts/server-key.mjs makes a key and its hash.

Rendering.description: How the forms placed on the site's pages are written.

IncludeAssetsAutomatically.description: Whether a form placed on a page writes the tags that load the website runtime, the base rules and its theme's stylesheet, once per page, when its placement does not say: true by default. Turned off, a placement writes them only when it asks (assets="true" on <jfb-render>, assets = true for the view component), and the site loads them itself, with a <jfb-assets> in its layout for example.

Files.description: Where uploaded files are kept, how large one may be, and which extensions no field takes.

Root.description: The folder the default store keeps the files in: ~/ followed by a path relative to the site's content root, or an absolute path, for example a folder that the servers of a load-balanced site share (the default lies on each server's own disk, and a load-balanced site that keeps it is told so at start-up). It must not lie inside the web root or contain it, as written or with its links followed: a site configured so does not start. Name the folder by its own path, because the check cannot see through an administrative share, a drive letter made with subst, a short 8.3 name or a link inside the web root that points to the folder.

MaxFileBytes.description: The most bytes any uploaded file may have, 1 to 999,999,999,999,999: 50 MiB unless the site sets another. A file field's own limit is held to it, and publishing refuses a field whose limit is higher. The upload endpoint sets each request's limit from its field's, a little above the file's for the parts around it; a server or proxy in front of the site with a lower limit of its own (IIS's maxAllowedContentLength, for example) refuses larger files first.

BlockedExtensions.description: The extensions no field takes, in lowercase letters and digits without the point, each once, such as dwg. A site's own list replaces the defaults (exe, dll, js, bat, cmd, ps1, sh, msi, html and svg), which apply while it lists none. Publishing refuses a field that lists one, and a field's groups of file types leave them out. Programs and scripts are refused by their first bytes, whatever their name.

Limits.description: Hard limits that editors cannot exceed.

Definitions.description: How large a form may be. Each limit is at least 1 and at most ten times its default. A lowered limit refuses to save a form above it, and forms stored above it keep working.

MaxBytes.description: The largest document, in UTF-8 bytes: 2 MB.

MaxGroups.description: Groups per form, on all pages.

MaxFields.description: Fields per form, counting the fields of repeatable groups and the rows of grids, which store like fields.

MaxRules.description: Rules per form: those of pages, groups, fields, actions and outcomes, and the form-level validation rules.

MaxTrackedClients.description: The most rate windows one server keeps for addresses, server keys and forms: 1,000 to 10,000,000, 100,000 by default. Past that, new ones share one overflow window per limit, so a flood of distinct addresses is limited and memory stays bounded.

ServerKeyFactor.description: How many times an address's limits a server key gets, since one server sends for all its visitors: 1 to 1,000, 10 by default. The limits of a form and of the site stay as they are.

Read.description: Reading a form, its markup and its options, and a post without JavaScript that only moves the visitor.

PerAddressPerMinute.description: Requests per minute from one address, or one server key.

PerAddressPerHour.description: Requests per hour from one address, or one server key.

PerAddressAndFormPerMinute.description: Requests per minute from one address, or one server key, about one form.

PerFormPerMinute.description: Requests per minute about one form, from anyone.

SitePerSecond.description: Requests per second to the whole site, from anyone; whatever the other limits do, this one holds.

Designer.description: Settings of field types and action types that the designer cannot change.

SettingLocks.description: Settings fixed for every form, for example the sender of every email action. Each names a kind, a type and a setting once.

items.description: A setting of a field type or an action type that is fixed in every form, for example { "kind": "action", "type": "email", "setting": "from", "value": "noreply@example.com", "hidden": true }. The designer shows it read-only, or not at all when hidden, a save that gives it another value is refused, and the site uses the locked value whatever a form says. The site does not start when a field type or its setting is missing, or the setting refuses the value.

Kind.description: Whether the lock is on a field type (field) or an action type (action), in any case.

Type.description: The type's alias, for example email: a letter, then letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_', at most 64 characters.

Setting.description: The setting's name at the top of the type's settings, for example from, spelt exactly as the type names it.

Value.description: The value every form uses, as text, at most 50,000 characters: a text, a number, a date, a time, a choice or a key as it is, true or false, a whole number as digits, a localised text as the text of every culture, and a list, an object or JSON written as JSON. Without one, the setting keeps its default.

Hidden.description: Hides the setting in the designer instead of showing it read-only.

Access.description: Who holds which permission: the global grants, set from the host.

Grants.description: The global grants, each naming a user group by its alias and the permissions it holds everywhere, for example { "group": "editor", "permissions": [ "viewEntries" ] }. With at least one, they replace the backoffice's global grants, which it then shows read-only; grants on folders and forms stay the backoffice's. Each group is listed once, and a permission comes with the one it needs (export with viewEntries).

items.description: A global grant from the host configuration.

Group.description: The user group's alias, for example editor. A group the site does not have is granted nothing.

Permissions.description: The permissions, in any case: design, manageActions, viewEntries, viewSensitive, editEntries, deleteEntries, export, manageLibrary, manageSettings, managePermissions or privacyTools.

Captcha.description: The keys of the captcha providers, which live only here.

SiteKey.description: The public key a page shows the captcha with.

SecretKey.description: The secret key tokens are verified with; it never leaves the server except to the provider.

VerifyAddress.description: Another address to verify tokens at, for a test host's stub; null for the provider's own.

UseRecaptchaNet.description: Whether reCAPTCHA is reached through recaptcha.net instead of google.com.

Webhooks.description: The other hosts Jiron Form Builder may call: JSON option lists now, webhooks later.

AllowedHosts.description: The hosts that may be called, each a host name such as events.example.com or an IP address, in any case, with no scheme, path or wildcard. A host alone is called on its scheme's standard port only (443, or 80 for http); to call it on another, name the port too: events.example.com:8443, or [2001:db8::1]:8443 for an IPv6 address. None by default, so nothing is called.

AllowHttp.description: Whether http addresses may be called too; only https by default.

LockedSections.description: Backoffice settings sections that are read-only: general, email, protection, files, privacy, access (every grant and restriction) or integrations, in any case.
